geometry_edits.rationale: Introduce a gym-appropriate roof section with daylight logic instead of a purely arched profile.
Keep the section aligned to a long-span hall direction.
Collapse the repeated array into one dominant mass to avoid a fragmented reading.
Reduce excessive curvature so the hall remains continuous and readable.

graph_edits.rationale: Reduce the arbitrary bend-driven fragmentation; a gym needs a clearer continuous hall axis.
Keep only a mild curvature so the dominant mass remains legible and continuous.
Remove the radial repetition that makes the volume read as a fragmented cluster rather than one hall.
Shift from a generic barrel to a more gym-appropriate daylight section that can read as span-bearing.
Preserve a clear longitudinal hall orientation consistent with a sports building.

rationale: The candidate reads as a compact, stepped object with some overall continuity in all four views, so it is not incoherent. However, the dominant gesture is weak for a gymnasium: the mass does not clearly resolve into one long-span hall with subordinate support, and the roof/section logic looks more like a generalized terraced block than an expressive sports section. The blue access edge is not met with a legible public void, court, or entry seam; instead the building remains largely sealed at ground level and semantically indifferent to the frontage. The silhouette is consistent but leans toward repetitive stepback fragments rather than a capacity-bearing continuous section. Repair integrity is good because the form stays enclosed and stable across views, but program appropriateness and section-program fit are low due to the absence of a clear hall span and public threshold.
